Definition: from G1722 and a derivative of G5453; implanted (figuratively):--engrafted.
BiblicalUsage: James calls the word of God the engrafted word in James 1:21 — planted in us like a cutting grafted into a tree, able to save our souls if we receive it with meekness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's word is not meant to sit on my shelf but to take root in me, and a grafted word bears fruit that my own words never could.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
